what_its_for: Trametinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of melanoma (skin cancer) that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is also used for some lung cancers and thyroid cancers. It works by blocking a protein called MEK that helps cancer cells grow and multiply. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or together with another medicine called dabrafenib.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or split the tablet. Take trametinib on an EMPTY STOMACH — at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level in your body. If you vomit after taking your dose, do NOT take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose as usual.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 2 mg taken by mouth ONCE daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on side effects or how well your body tolerates the medicine. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is MORE than 12 hours away. If your next dose is less than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store trametinib tablets in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep the tablets in the original bottle with the lid tightly closed. Keep the medicine away from moisture and light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after your last dose. Avoid breastfeeding while taking trametinib and for 4 months after stopping. Avoid prolonged sun exposure — wear sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors, as this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to the sun. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting trametinib, as many drugs can interact with it.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden vision changes or loss of vision, severe eye pain or redness, chest pain, shortness of breath, or a pounding heartbeat (signs of heart problems), fever of 101°F or higher (especially if also taking dabrafenib), unusual bleeding or bruising, signs of a skin rash that is severe or blistering, swelling of your legs or ankles, sudden severe headache, confusion, or weakness (signs of a possible brain problem), severe diarrhea, nausea, or vomiting that you cannot control, muscle pain or weakness, or signs of a new skin cancer such as a new wart, sore, or bump on the skin.
when_it_works: Trametinib does not work right away. It may take several weeks to months before your doctor can tell if the medicine is helping. Your doctor will order regular blood tests and scans to check how well the treatment is working. Do not stop taking the medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you do not feel different.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use trametinib if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for 4 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment and for 4 months after. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for 4 months after stopping. Older adults (65 and over): Trametinib can be used in older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. Children: The safety and effectiveness of trametinib in children has not been fully established for most uses. Your doctor will determine if it is appropriate.
